`SourceCurrentStoredCallbackChildContexts.filter_row` proves exact RowAt
preservation through actual root self filtering under Normal and availability.
RowAt can descend through original unions and original stored Mu bodies.
The existing literal-row filter theorem does not cover that second case.
The new proof separates a literal row from a literal whole-Mu atom with an
internal RowAt. The filter preserves the same Mu atom and its unchanged body.
No unfolding or observational row transport is substituted for this step.

`filter_child` keeps the exact original full row, symbol, guard, arity,
original child index and supported lexical call interval. It recomputes the
strict size bound for the original child relative to the raw callback value.
It places no bound on the generated child. The retained child calls are
calls from stored-body unfolding. They are not calls that execute the raw
callback value at that earlier entry heap.

`written_child` selects one raw_contexts witness from the strong writer.
Mu payload injectivity identifies the same entry, body, depth and ordinary
value with that publication. The result retains the actual historical Syntax
build, root filter and raw return heap. At the final reader it retains the
original lexical Context, available raw result, actual Keeps interval and
exact warm build/filter replay. It then lifts the Child anchor to that raw
result. It does not identify the publication expression with a later native
callback. The old physical writer alone would not supply these contexts.

`head_child` retains the same chosen Mu, prior Chain, actual unfold, literal
suffix, full row, child index and issued-name writer. It derives final
readiness from actual Head effects, then supplies the actual callback
receipts and lifted Child. Semantic readiness, costs, initial availability,
closed input, completed Head and an actual empty-to-entry Path remain explicit.
It does not assert availability or an overall execute call for the raw value
at the earlier stored-unfold entry.

Four public declarations pass complete proof output with all eight printer
settings and only standard axioms. Strict production3 has an empty log.
The full default build passes 3475 jobs and 73974 axiom checks. Its only
warning is the existing ClosedCompletion unused-input warning.

Its separate structural-row check crosses two opaque Mu bodies. That filter
is a pass-through on Mu. It does not test root-union removal. Strict fixture3
has an empty log. Full1 passes all eight printer settings and standard axioms.

### Strongest proved system statements

Fresh construction always finishes in the Lean model. Under the stated
guard conditions, it represents exactly the finite trees in the independent
syntax semantics. The general completed reduction law is
`L(input) intersect Sat(inherited) <= L(result) <= L(input)`.
It does not assert that every output satisfies arbitrary inherited constraints.

The top root-language theorem is
`SourceCurrentConstructedRootCall.root_call`. Start with actual closed fresh
construction and original-field allocation that covers every expression
guard. The equality interner must be valid. Logical caller and memo startup
are empty. Inheritance is the actual empty value. If the supported bounded
root call returns and Fits, carrier and scheduled Room hold, then its result
is available and, for every ambient interpretation,
`L(result) = evaluate(original expression)`.
The theorem derives the logical initialization and guard context. It does
not prove general root completion, concrete Haskell startup or integer bounds.

The modeled reference and optimized Sized paths complete with the same result
and cache, including errors, under their construction and annotation premises.
If they return a query API, its size classes, counts, rank/unrank and enumeration
prefixes are exact. Not every input is proved to return an API. Read
`lean/notes-current-system-claim.md` for the complete current contracts.
